prompt: A class admits tree-models with a uniform height bound and a uniform finite number of leaf colours. Its graph vertices are the leaves; adjacency depends only on the two colours and their tree distance. What property is described?

answers.explanation: Both height and colour count are uniform across the class. The tree is a model of adjacency, not a subgraph that must contain the graph.
Treewidth uses overlapping bags, not an adjacency interpretation on coloured leaves.
A height-one model with one colour already represents arbitrarily large cliques.
The same height-one models can represent cliques of every size.
Treedepth uses containment in a forest closure and excludes arbitrarily large cliques at a fixed bound.
Bounded clique-width imposes no uniform tree-model height; paths separate the two properties.
Twin-width controls red degree during contractions and does not impose this height condition.
Neighbourhood diversity corresponds to height-one tree-models; bounded shrubdepth permits larger fixed heights.
Paths have bounded linear clique-width but unbounded shrubdepth.
Merge-width controls local reachability of resolved pairs, not bounded-height leaf models.

sources.title: Ganian et al. — Shrub-depth: Capturing Height of Dense Graphs, §§2–4
Dreier & Toruńczyk — Merge-width and First-Order Model Checking, Definitions 3.1–3.2 and §7 (June 2026 version)
